done_when: Close writes the proof list from the tests it ran and their results, and the worker only names which Done-when item each test proves; a named test close did not run shows as not run, and a name close cannot match to its own run's results is marked not checked

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. The new fallback copies lines that contain no Python pytest name into the published proof list and adds `not checked`. A client using JavaScript tests can therefore publish an unrun `src/greet.test.ts` or `__tests__/greeting.js` as a named test. The new command test explicitly expects both names to remain in the published list (tests/test_close_checks_named_tests.py:103-104). The `not checked` marker is new evidence beyond the earlier JavaScript finding, but the Done-when requirement still says the list never names a test that did not run.
findings.title: Not done: Proof lists retain names of tests Close did not run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. If the worker names `tests/test_greeting.py::test_case` and Close runs only `test_case[new]`, this branch strips the parameter ID when comparing the sole match and publishes the whole function as `passed`. It neither names the case that ran nor shows the count of cases run, although another parameter case remains unrun. The command test covers individual parameter IDs and a whole file, but never a bare parameterized function.
findings.title: Not done: A partially run parameterized test is reported as passed

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 2, reversible): one last round on the two cases workers hit every day — names wrapped in Markdown code marks match like plain names, and each test counts once with a failed teardown counted as that test's failure. Anything further in review.py is accepted as a follow-up.

why: Workers write proof lists by hand, and about one review round in five is a gate on a missing or wrong test name in that list
